body.statement: Suppose \(d_{ei}=d_{ej}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\). For every \(\beta,\gamma\ne0\) and \(u,w,z>0\), the fork \(i\to j\), \(i\to k\), with coefficients \(\beta,\gamma\) and reference innovation variances \((u,w,z)\) in coordinate order \((i,j,k)\), has exactly the same covariance in every environment as the chain \(j\to i\to k\) with coefficients \(\beta u/(\beta^2u+w),\gamma\) and reference innovation variances \((uw/(\beta^2u+w),\beta^2u+w,z)\). Thus the two nonisomorphic exact supports form a positive-dimensional twin family. Setting \(\beta=\gamma=u=w=z=1\) gives the covariance block \(\begin{psmallmatrix}d_{ei}&d_{ei}&d_{ei}\\d_{ei}&2d_{ei}&d_{ei}\\d_{ei}&d_{ei}&d_{ei}+d_{ek}\end{psmallmatrix}\). For \(p=2\), deleting vertex \(k\) gives reverse one-edge twins; for \(p>3\), adjoining independent vertices embeds the family into the larger exact-support strata.
body.justification: The positive fork--chain family proves necessity without zero innovations or vanished displayed edges.
body.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Appendix A, perturbs covariance-difference diagonalizers; it does not exhibit nonisomorphic acyclic models whose full covariance families coincide under tied multiplicative profiles.
body.consumer: Experimental designers receive an explicit impossibility certificate for any tied schedule pair.
